responsibility: Read-only presentation layer for a completed run. Assembles the opportunity matrix view, the genre/tag summary table, the top-N case studies with a short rationale, and the fixed interpretive caveats. Returns objects for the UI to render; writes no files and no database rows.
changelog: 0.2.0 - is_partial is now derived from run_stages rather than inferred from runs.status, and RunReport carries the stage list so the UI can name which stage is missing (ADR-014, ADR-016). No new runs.status value was introduced; is_partial remains the only UI-visible partial/complete distinction (ADR-016).

0.3.0 - select_case_studies now returns CaseStudySelection (case_studies plus an archetype_cap_relaxed flag) instead of a bare list, giving the one-time diversity-cap relaxation an explicit, testable signal instead of only being detectable indirectly by the caller.
design_notes: Deliberately independent of the analysis module so any historical run can be rendered even after analysis logic changes shape. It reads persisted analysis_results and games_enriched only.
Case-study rationale text is assembled from stored numeric fields through fixed templates. No free-form generated prose, so a rendered claim always traces back to a stored value.
Every revenue or sales figure is rendered as a band with its caveat attached. A point estimate must never be displayed alone.
Partial-run handling is expressed through is_partial, not through an extra runs.status value. The run status vocabulary stays pending/running/succeeded/failed/cancelled (ADR-016).

public_interface.name: load_run_report
public_interface.signature: def load_run_report(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str) -> RunReport
public_interface.description: Single call that assembles everything the Analysis Detail page needs, including the run's stage list. Raises ReportNotAvailable only when the run_id itself is unknown; a run with missing or incomplete stages returns a partial report instead of raising.

public_interface.name: is_partial_run
public_interface.description: The single definition of partial: {s.stage for s in stages if s.status == 'succeeded'} != {'acquisition', 'enrichment', 'analysis'}. Independent of runs.status by construction, so a run that is still running, was cancelled, failed, or crashed with the process all resolve to partial through the same rule. missing_stages is the complement of that set, in pipeline order.

public_interface.name: FunnelSummary
public_interface.description: Makes the coarse filter's hard boundary visible in the UI, per ARCHITECTURE.md limitation 7. detail_fetched / detail_failed expose per-app fetch coverage, which is how a degraded but still 'succeeded' acquisition becomes visible to the user (ADR-016).

public_interface.name: build_opportunity_matrix_view
public_interface.signature: def build_opportunity_matrix_view(matrix: pd.DataFrame, *, min_n: int | None = None, sort_by: str = 'opportunity_score') -> pd.DataFrame
public_interface.description: Display-ready frame: rounded values, human-readable column names, sample size always present as a column.

public_interface.name: build_tag_summary_table
public_interface.signature: def build_tag_summary_table(tag_summary: pd.DataFrame, *, top_n: int = 100) -> pd.DataFrame

public_interface.name: select_case_studies
public_interface.signature: def select_case_studies(enriched: pd.DataFrame, assignments: pd.DataFrame, *, top_n: int = 15, max_per_archetype: int = 2, max_per_developer: int = 1) -> CaseStudySelection
public_interface.description: Ranks by effort_adjusted_return within the simple subset, then enforces archetype and developer diversity caps so the list does not collapse onto one studio or one genre. Returns CaseStudySelection rather than a bare list so the one-time max_per_archetype relaxation (see edge_cases) has an explicit signal; load_run_report unwraps case_studies and, when archetype_cap_relaxed, appends an extra Caveat.

public_interface.name: build_rationale
public_interface.signature: def build_rationale(row: pd.Series, archetype_label: str) -> str
public_interface.description: Template-filled sentence naming the concrete signals that put the game on the list (review volume, positivity, price, install size, achievement count, developer catalog size). Hedged wording only: 'plausibly small in scope', never 'took two weeks to build'.

public_interface.name: interpretive_caveats
public_interface.description: Returns the fixed caveat set mirroring ARCHITECTURE.md 'Known Limitations' items 1-7. The UI is required to render these on every result surface.

public_interface.name: partial_run_caveat
public_interface.signature: def partial_run_caveat(missing_stages: Sequence[str], run: RunRecord) -> Caveat
public_interface.description: Additional caveat appended when is_partial is True, naming the stages that did not succeed and surfacing runs.error_message. Severity 'warning' for a cancelled run, 'error' for a failed one.

public_interface.name: headline_metrics
public_interface.description: Small summary for the run list: catalog size, candidate count, detail fetch coverage, simple subset size, top archetype label, run duration.

invariants: The module performs no writes of any kind
is_partial has exactly one definition, is_partial_run over run_stages; no other code path may compute it from runs.status
Whenever is_partial is True the caveat list contains partial_run_caveat naming the missing stages
Every displayed sales or revenue number is accompanied by its estimate band and the relevant caveat key
Every aggregate row displays its sample size
Case-study rationale uses hedged language about effort; it may state observed signals but never asserts development time or cost
A run that stopped mid-pipeline still renders whatever stages completed
edge_cases: Run exists but no stage has been attempted yet -> is_partial=True, missing_stages lists all three, all frames empty, no exception
Run status is 'running' -> partial report with whatever results are already committed; the write-ordering rule (ADR-016) guarantees that a stage reported as succeeded has its data committed
Run failed -> partial report plus the run's error_message surfaced through partial_run_caveat
Run cancelled -> same as failed but with severity 'warning', since cancellation is a user action rather than a defect
A stage row exists with status 'running' but no live worker (process died) -> treated as not succeeded, hence partial; reconciliation of runs.status is orchestration's job, not reporting's
Acquisition succeeded but detail_failed is a large share of candidate_count -> run is not partial, the coverage numbers are surfaced in FunnelSummary and headline_metrics instead
analysis_results present but empty (too little data) -> empty frames with an explanatory caveat, not an exception
Fewer candidates than top_n for case studies -> return what exists
Diversity caps making top_n unreachable -> fill up to the cap, then relax max_per_archetype once and record that it was relaxed
Missing optional fields on an older run (schema evolved) -> render the field as unavailable rather than raising
NaN or None in a displayed numeric column -> rendered as an explicit unavailable marker, never as 0

unit: load_run_report on a fixture database returns fully populated frames and is_partial=False when all three stages succeeded
load_run_report raises ReportNotAvailable for an unknown run_id
is_partial_run returns False only for the exact set of three succeeded stages, and True for every other combination including an extra unknown stage name
a run whose analysis stage is missing yields is_partial=True and missing_stages == ['analysis']
a still-running run yields is_partial=True without raising
a cancelled run produces partial_run_caveat with severity 'warning'; a failed run with severity 'error'
select_case_studies returns fewer than top_n when the pool is smaller, without padding
build_rationale output contains the stored numeric signals and contains no unhedged effort claim (asserted against a forbidden-phrase list)
interpretive_caveats returns one caveat per ARCHITECTURE.md limitation and the keys are stable
NaN values render as the unavailable marker rather than 0
integration: load_run_report over the fixture database matches an expected snapshot of the rendered tables, for both a complete and a stage-truncated run

non_goals: No file output (no CSV, PDF or Markdown export in v1)
No recomputation of any metric; everything comes from stored values
No Streamlit imports; the module must be usable and testable headless
No reconciliation or repair of run / stage status; reporting reads status, it never corrects it
open_questions: Default top_n for case studies (15 proposed)
Whether a CSV export button is wanted in v1, which would make this module write files
